decisions.rationale: Verified. The 'o1 the ON condition' distractor feedback says ON books.author_id = books.author_id 'pairs every author with every book'. A book whose author_id is NULL pairs with no author, because NULL = NULL is null (cited comparison documentation), which is this module's own NULL rule. Fix the feedback wording in artifact.gift, for example 'so every author pairs with every book that has an author_id'.

Reproduced, the same defect as C2E-JOIN-01. 'ORDER BY instructor_id' gives the ambiguous ERROR, explain suggests s.instructor_id, and following it gives 'missing FROM-clause entry for table "s"'. Fix SQLCHK.explain in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js to use an alias from the failing statement's FROM/JOIN items (see C2E-ANTI-05).

Reproduced back to back. The task-literal 'ORDER BY instructor_id, course_id' gives 'column reference "instructor_id" is ambiguous', the explain line suggests 's.instructor_id', and running that gives 'missing FROM-clause entry for table "s"'. This is on the activity's main path. Fix: in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js, build the example from an alias the failing statement defines (see C2E-ANTI-05). In the task step and hint 2, say 'the instructor's instructor_id' and 'the course's course_id', so qualifying is part of the instruction. The recap's '(s.student_id)' example is fine, because it is generic.

Verified: html-artifact-contract.md says 'at most 120 words per teach step', and DESIGN.md says 'Concept (≤120 words)'. I counted Activity 2's [data-pep-teaching] text, leaving out pre, figure, table and details, at 160 words. It packs the inner join, ON, a review link, aliases, qualifying, the ambiguous ERROR, duplicate matches, dropped rows and a JDBC aside into one step. Fix: cut to 120 or fewer, for example move the JDBC sentence to the On the job card and shorten the alias and qualifying paragraph. Keep the definition of qualifying, because the explain translation and the task rely on it.

Verified strings. The authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/build.mjs badge reads 'Practice editor: follows PostgreSQL on this page's sample tables' and the status span reads 'SQL practice editor'. In authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js, EDITOR.language='PostgreSQL server' feeds the shell's Output header '(lesson simulator, not real PostgreSQL server)', while SQLCHK.explain says 'PostgreSQL cannot tell which one you mean' / 'PostgreSQL would stop with the ERROR'. The shell's empty Problems text is 'No problems found by the lesson checker', which also uses B4 grader vocabulary. C2 F5 says a page never says both 'not real' and 'PostgreSQL rejected'. In-loop fix, page-owned bytes only: use one name ('practice editor') in the build.mjs badge and status span, choose EDITOR.language so the shell header reads consistently with it, and word the explain lines as what 'a real PostgreSQL server' would report. The shell's 'lesson simulator, not real' prefix and its 'No problems found by the lesson checker' sentence are engine.js shell bytes: record a recipe finding. On this page the conflict is sharpest, because the ambiguous-column translation says 'PostgreSQL cannot tell which one you mean' under a header that says 'not real PostgreSQL server', the residue of the new-learner F5 finding.

Verified. Activity 3 step 2 gives the SELECT list as code ('i.name AS instructor and c.title AS course'), step 1 fixes the table order, and hint 1 repeats it. The editor alt and topic.js sql[3].fallback also spell 'selecting i.name AS instructor and c.title AS course'. Fix: state the output columns by meaning (a column instructor with the instructor's name, a column course with the course title) and let the learner choose aliases. Apply the same rewording to the alt, fallback, static exercise text and artifact.md. Keep hint 2 a reasoning step about the linking column. The check already accepts any aliases, because it tests output names only.

Verified. Every unreadable statement, the empty-file prompt and every real subset limit reach the shell as kind 'limit' from the adapter's check() in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/engine.js; I reproduced 'SELEC * FROM students;', a missing comma between two VALUES rows, a missing semicolon before a second SELECT and the untouched starter, all kind 'limit'. authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js relabels 'limit' as 'Not in this practice editor', and LIMITS item 4 in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/build.mjs plus every page's Sources footer ('not as invalid PostgreSQL') say that label never means the SQL is wrong. The label is page-owned, so it is fixable in scope. Acceptable fix: in controller.js, wrap EDITOR.check (EDITOR is Object.create of the adapter) and re-kind problems by message into three classes. Real subset limits (WITH, psql meta-commands, CREATE TABLE and so on) keep 'Not in this practice editor'. Unreadable statements ('could not read the statement near', 'could not read one starting') get a learner label such as 'Check your SQL'. The empty-file prompt gets its own neutral label. Message matching is feasible: I checked that real limits carry their own messages ('WITH queries are outside this practice editor', 'CREATE is not available here', 'Transactions are outside this practice editor', 'COPY runs on the database server', and the psql meta-command text), distinct from the unreadable-statement messages. Never use the adapter's own 'Lesson check' (B4), and never use kind 'hint', because the shell blocks Run only on non-hint problems. Run gating, the 'limit' notRun status and onSqlRun's 'did not use up a try' path must stay exactly as they are (E2 is pending). Reword LIMITS item 4 and the footer sentence in each src/<topic>.body.html and artifact.md to match. The minimum acceptable fix, if message matching seems too brittle, is one neutral label covering both cases, with LIMITS and footer sentences that no longer say the SQL is fine. Shell wording stays a recipe finding.

Verified in the page simulator. A missing semicolon at the end of line 3 is reported at Ln 4 near "select", and a missing comma at the end of line 2 of a multi-row VALUES is reported at Ln 3 near "(" (policy 1.3, E5). Where the location comes from (the adapter's Limit token line in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/engine.js) is out of scope, so record a recipe finding: the adapter should report the end of the previous token. In-loop fix, per policy 1.3's second bullet: in the same controller.js check wrapper, when the message is 'could not read the statement near' and the token is first on its line, either point Ln at the previous non-blank line or append 'If this line looks right, check the end of the line before it for a missing comma or semicolon.' Wording and location only; run gating does not change.

Verified. Activity 2 hint 2 says 'ORDER BY takes two keys separated by a comma', and the sql[3] note says 'add the course's id as a second key', on a page whose joins are built on primary and foreign keys (B1/D3). Fix: 'sort columns' in both places, in body.html and topic.js.

Checked the bytes. The retry distractor 'enrollments LEFT JOIN students WHERE students.student_id IS NULL' and its explanation in src/inner-and-left-joins.topic.js ('this looks for enrollments whose student is missing, a different question; with these tables it returns no rows') need only two ideas: that LEFT JOIN fills the right table's columns with NULL when nothing matches, which this page teaches in Activity 3 and the recap, and IS NULL, which handling-nulls-coalesce-and-case teaches earlier in topicOrder. No sentence needs the later topic's anti-join concept or name, so B2 holds. Rejecting a distractor because it can be reasoned out from taught pieces is not required by D3.

Verified. CONF in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/build.mjs prints Low / Medium / High, but DESIGN.md (Assessment: options, confidence, feedback) sets "Guessing", "Fairly sure", "Certain". In authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js, checkPredict writes 'Your guess was not this time', and summarize() joins open activities as 'Activity '+open.join(' and '), which gives 'Activity 2 and 3 and 4 are'. Fix, wording only: in CONF, use the DESIGN.md labels (the radio values low/medium/high may stay). calibration() echoes the raw value ('Your confidence: medium'), so map it to the shown label. Write 'Your guess was not right this time', and join a list as 'Activities 2, 3 and 4 are' (singular 'Activity 2 is').

Reproduced at 570x1000 under file:// and over http://127.0.0.1: scrollY 157, exactly the top of #activity-1. At 1280 px it is 121 on inner-and-left-joins and 0 where the document fits. Cause confirmed: with history.replaceState stubbed out, scrollY stays 0. The last line of authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js calls go(...,'replace'), whose history.replaceState(#activity-1) runs during parsing. It does not throw, and the browser's load-time scroll-to-fragment then scrolls to #activity-1, so F1 fails on the narrow frame (G7). Fix in controller.js: on first load with no #activity-N in the URL, do not write a hash (call go with no history mode), or write it after load and keep scroll at 0. Keep the hash behaviour for later navigation. Measured in headless Chromium only; check the platform embed after the fix.
